items.headline: Fed decision becomes the dominant cross-asset catalyst
items.summary: The Fed is widely expected to raise rates by 25 bp on September 16, its first hike since 2023. Barron's September 16 Daily centers on the decision and the policy path after it; the decision had not occurred at the AGCI cutoff.
items.whyItMatters: With the 10-year Treasury recently above 5%, guidance and the reaction of real yields matter more than the well-telegraphed first move. Avoid a concentrated duration bet before the decision.

items.headline: Saudi Arabia builds an Oman workaround for disrupted crude exports
items.summary: Saudi Arabia is offering more crude to Asian buyers through ship-to-ship loading off Sohar, Oman, while Yanbu loadings remain halted after damage to the East-West pipeline. Some European September cargoes were cancelled or delayed.
items.whyItMatters: The workaround reduces immediate tail risk but confirms that the physical export system remains impaired. Keep a moderate energy hedge without extrapolating the recent oil rally indefinitely.

items.headline: SK Hynix and Intel explore U.S. memory manufacturing partnership
items.summary: SK Hynix and Intel are in early-stage talks over U.S. memory production, including possible use of Intel's Ohio capacity or a joint venture. No agreement is finalized.
items.whyItMatters: AI memory demand, tariff pressure and supply-chain localization could improve utilization of Intel assets and expand U.S. HBM/DRAM capacity, but the talks are preliminary and should not be capitalized as contracted earnings.

items.headline: BOJ expected to lift policy rate to 1.25%
items.summary: The BOJ is expected to raise its policy rate to 1.25% on September 18 as oil and yen weakness sustain inflation risk. The decision is still pending.
items.whyItMatters: Further Japanese normalization can support JPY and pressure global carry trades and duration. Review unhedged Japan exposure and funding assumptions.

items.headline: Euro-zone wage growth continues to cool
items.summary: Euro-zone labor-cost growth slowed to 3.1% year over year in Q2, while negotiated wage indicators point to only a modest pickup into early 2027.
items.whyItMatters: Cooling wages partially offsets the inflationary energy shock and argues against assuming an extended ECB hiking cycle solely from headline inflation.
